pull_request.body:
## Executive summary

Retain the research tracks comparing **MAG-01–05** as isolated DES-004 magnetic-layout prototypes; **MAG-06 remains withdrawn** following expert direction. No topology is selected and no production geometry is changed.

The [2026-09-24 expert response](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-magnet-sizing-review.md) implements review-directed vessel gaps, **30 MJ/m³ stored-energy/cold-volume sizing**, and a **hard 5 T central-field cap**, with 1–4 T preferred. Current vacuum controls remain at 3 T and retain homogeneous winding-pack current density. The rules are recorded in AGENTS.md, a central policy, field/layout validators and CI for current and future studies.

| Main-coil family | Vacuum stored energy | Cold-mass radial bounds | Vessel radial bounds | Cold / vessel full length |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| Inner: MAG-01/02/05 | 132.576 MJ | 1.327800–1.405769 m | 1.240000–1.559419 m | 6.60 / 7.10 m |
| Outer: MAG-03/04 | 3624.582 MJ | 4.586700–4.898584 m | 4.300000–5.400309 m | 13.00 / 13.60 m |

**Integration consequence:** the outer-family vessel grows by 0.600309 m radially. MAG-03/04 muon hosts, nested radial budgets and trial steel bands move outward by that amount, preserving their depths and 0.15 m vessel-to-host gap. Overall outer radii become 8.100309 / 10.600309 m. Stepped endcap fronts, beam apertures, tracker and calorimeters stay at their retained study coordinates. All five updated layouts pass positive-intersection and containment checks.

![Updated five-option composite layouts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/docs/design/figures/DES-004-muon-envelopes-comparison-rz.png)

## Expert comments and implementation

- **Axial lengths:** previous end allowances were planning choices, not engineered vessel-length estimates. The current model explicitly sets cold length equal to winding length, with 0.25 / 0.30 m per-end allowances. End supports, leads, shields, cooldown movement and closures still need engineering.
- **Inner radial gap:** enforce `RCMi = 1.065 RVi + 0.0072 m`.
- **Cold thickness:** iterate winding geometry, its uniform current normalization and cold-mass outer radius until calculated stored energy equals 30 MJ/m³ times the annular cold volume. Retain the earlier 2:1 winding/support radial split as an explicit provisional closure.
- **Outer radial gap:** provisionally interpret the undefined `RCM` as `RCMi`, giving `RVo = RCMo + 1.75 (RCMi − RVi)`. **Expert confirmation remains requested.**
- **Field:** reject nonfinite central fields or magnitudes above 5 T. Complete installed fields must obey that cap after adding iron or other magnets; a main-coil vacuum control cannot certify the total field or peak conductor margin.

The new energy calculation integrates the complete vacuum field through the equivalent current/vector-potential source integral, with axial separation integrated analytically. It includes fringe/return energy and avoids a finite map cutoff or a uniform-bore proxy. [Sizing input/code/results](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/docs/validation/DES-004-magnet-sizing.json) retain provenance and refinement. [Reproduction commands](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/tools/magnetic_study/README.md) require no new numerical dependency beyond NumPy.

## Evidence and limits

At the September 24 scientific evidence revision, passed locally: **26 magnetic tests, 26 dashboard tests, 15 logging tests, 5 node-preflight tests and 14 JavaScript assertions**, dashboard validation/build, session validation, input/code hashes and whitespace checks. Energy tests include an independent infinite-solenoid field-energy limit, analytic axial integration, B²/geometric scaling, refinement and rejection cases. All twelve updated field benchmark samples and all five composite geometries pass. Magnetic tests now run in hosted CI.

These are conditional **vacuum main-coil** results. Installed calorimeter/support steel affects every physical candidate; MAG-02/04 need nonlinear iron solutions and MAG-05 needs explicit toroid windings, coupled energy and cold-volume accounting. Inner pack-average J becomes 49.643 A/mm², requiring conductor/protection review. No structural adequacy, peak-field margin, standalone muon performance or full transport map is demonstrated.

The earlier thin-sheet and finite-pack evidence remains historical. The 2026-09-22 finite-winding benchmark is unchanged; new field evidence is separately named. Prior composite reports/drawings remain in Git. The old MAG-06 card is archived, not promoted back into the active comparison.

## Synchronization and accounting — 2026-10-12

Resolved all 26 conflict paths through an ordinary merge of `main` at `ed30e63fb0ab30b66d4084a9058906929006f792`. Retained both source catalogues and all review records by stable ID, including exact reviewed revisions and approval states. All 78 magnetic-study files are byte-identical to the previous PR head. Magnetic regression tests now run in the current Project validation workflow; the retired progress-dashboard workflow remains removed.

The merge brings existing canonical token backfills into this branch: **36 disjoint turns across 11 research session records, 56,250,297 input + 211,577 output = 56,461,874 observed tokens**. They were already counted on main and are not counted again. The device audit found no additional attributable historical PR6 counters. **Token usage for the September 28 PR6 merge-maintenance session is still unavailable on this device**, as are final counters for this active update turn. The now-completed preceding PR62 synchronization turn adds 3,486,578 tokens to its own original session, separate from magnetic research. [Curated audit](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/research/magnetic-configurations/logs/usage/USAGE-2026-10-12-pr6-accounting-audit.json).

Current local validation: **108 Python tests passed** (26 magnetic, 11 envelope, 28 project-record, 33 session-logging and 10 token-site); project records validation; token-site validation/build; session validation and accounting summary. Full whitespace scans report only inherited generated SVG whitespace, verified byte-for-byte against the respective parents; the edited workflow, index, catalogues and records pass. Hosted checks are reported on the published revision.

## Review boundary

This update makes the research record compatible with current main; **no topology decision, selection, design approval or sign-off is recorded**. DES-004 remains DRAFT, the studies remain isolated PROTOTYPE work, and the historical CHANGES_REQUESTED review is preserved. PR6 itself is not merged by this update.

Scientific follow-up remains the provisional `RCMi` interpretation, axial allowances, winding/support closure, conductor margin and complete installed-field validation. Final human sign-off remains with `asalzburger-review`. Related: DES-004, ADR-006 and muon-performance issue #9. Scientific evidence target remains `2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645`; closing the issue or merging the research record does not confer approval.

- why does the barrel part grow so much, that the endcap calorimeter / Muon System volume gap becomes bigger and bigger ?

- what drives this and can it be avoided ?

Same question here, the gap between the Calo/Muon endcap is growing, but seems not to be filled with anything.

Please double-check this.
An alternative would be to not make the Muon endcap box shaped but at smaller inner radius first (within the barrel), and then increase the outer radius to match or supersed the barrel radius.

The question here is if the return field of an outer solenoid would support any of this or if this really requires a dedicated Muon System magnetic setup.

Of course the capability of ATLAS to do muon-only fit is great, but it comes with a price of complexity.

Let our physics/validation agent ponder a bit on that and make a Pro/Contra list as an issue.

There a few question to be answered.

The growing gap came from our rectangular-envelope convention: we moved the entire endcap front whenever the barrel became longer. We had not identified a physical requirement for that extra empty axial space. This has now been changed in all six candidates.

Each endcap has a narrower upstream section inside the barrel, then widens downstream. Inner-solenoid options start at |z|=6.35 m, 0.15 m beyond HCal; outer-solenoid options start at 6.95 m, 0.15 m beyond the outer-coil assembly. Thus barrel length no longer sets the upstream endcap front. The outer-family HCal-to-muon separation remains 0.75 m because this proposal stays beyond the coil's axial extent; the coil does not occupy that whole bore, and detailed service/end-structure allocation remains open.

All six composite layouts pass positive-intersection checks. These are provisional envelopes, not demonstrated installation clearances. [Revised drawings](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/f6a5caea1720d404e640bfe4f86de9c43cc17fa6/docs/design/figures/DES-004-muon-envelopes-comparison-rz.png) and [interface rationale](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/f6a5caea1720d404e640bfe4f86de9c43cc17fa6/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-envelope-coordination.md).

Double-checked: the former extra gap was not justified by an allocated component. We have replaced the single endcap box with a stepped host, reclaiming upstream space independently of barrel length. The inner-family front is now at |z|=6.35 m and the outer-family front at 6.95 m. The trial 0.15 m boundary allowances still need service/shielding validation; coloured muon space includes magnet/support/service needs and is not entirely chamber volume.

The retained 0.40 m aperture also matters: an eta=3.5 prompt straight ray enters the inner-family host near |z|=6.617 m, not at the 6.35 m front. This limitation is explicit in the [revised allocation rationale](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/f6a5caea1720d404e640bfe4f86de9c43cc17fa6/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-muon-envelope-amendments.md).

Implemented this approach in the research proposals: a narrower upstream section extends inside the barrel, followed by the full-radius downstream section. Specifically the upstream radial ranges are 0.4–4.2 m for inner-solenoid layouts and 0.4–4.8 m for outer-solenoid layouts. The barrel and endcap coordinates are independently specified; collision checks enforce compatibility rather than a rule equating their lengths.

[Six revised layouts](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/f6a5caea1720d404e640bfe4f86de9c43cc17fa6/docs/design/figures/DES-004-muon-envelopes-comparison-rz.png). End-return coils/steel, measurements and services still need explicit subdivisions within those hosts. No baseline replacement or design sign-off is implied.

Agreed; the redesign is now represented explicitly, rather than using the inherited envelope as a reason to reject MAG-03. Its muon barrel starts at r=4.95 m outside the proposed coil, extends to 7.50 m, and has a stepped endcap starting at |z|=6.95 m.

We also coordinated reuse of the absent inner-coil space with the tracker, calorimeter and muon engineers: ECal barrel r=1.30–1.66 m, ECal endcap outer radius 1.66 m, HCal barrel r=1.76–4.20 m. Tracker/services and nominal ECal thickness are retained; HCal gains 0.40 m of assembly capacity. The endcap ECal radius changes to avoid an overlap with the inward HCal barrel.

[Coordinated proposal and alternatives](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/f6a5caea1720d404e640bfe4f86de9c43cc17fa6/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-inner-space-reallocation.md). Overlap checks and sampled calorimeter-host paths pass; cryostat fit, material, field and performance remain open. The previous conflict applies to the unchanged E1-R2 host, not this amended proposal.

The proposal is now more concrete, but we cannot yet claim demonstrated viability. MAG-06 reserves r=4.95–8.10 m for return-field measurements, 8.10–8.60 m for the return-coil assembly and 8.60–8.85 m for outer routes. Its stepped endcap provides additional upstream space from |z|=6.95 m; only its full-radius section remains limited to 9.0–10.9 m.

The existing flux-area screen shows that the annulus could carry the illustrative uniform-return flux at about 1.48 T. This is conditional arithmetic, not a finite-coil field solution. The 4th Concept precedent is conceptual, and its quoted angular reach does not establish our eta=3/3.5 requirement.

The next discriminating calculation is a finite main+opposed-return solenoid model, followed by explicit end-coil variants: report central field, signed bending between candidate stations, external field, current demands and sensitivity to current mismatch. End-coil/support/service fit and later steel, force, energy/protection and material studies must follow. No such dual-coil calculation has been run here, so this remains an open feasibility question rather than a resolved review point. [Current card and test sequence](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/f6a5caea1720d404e640bfe4f86de9c43cc17fa6/docs/design/options/DES-004-MAG-06.md).

The Physics/Performance agent has reviewed this and prepared the requested pro/con study: [issue #9](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/issues/9).

An independent muon momentum measurement does not inherently require a separately powered muon magnet. An instrumented solenoid return field can supply the bending, provided it is sampled by independent muon measurements. MAG-04 has a built-topology precedent in CMS; that does not transfer CMS performance to our geometry. For MAG-03 without a dedicated yoke, useful fringe/return curvature between the stations remains unproven. Main-field bending followed only by an outgoing segment cannot by itself provide an unconstrained muon-only momentum measurement.

The issue compares return iron, toroids and active return, including scattering/material, forward field orientation, alignment, station leverage and magnet complexity. It separates tracker-only, unconstrained standalone, vertex-constrained and combined fits, and specifies the field/measurement tests needed before selecting a topology. No numerical performance ranking is claimed.

The physics agent's assessment is now recorded in [issue #9](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/issues/9), including MAG-01 as the compact control. Its standalone capability is neither demonstrated nor ruled out: the test is whether curvature between independent outer measurements supplies usable momentum information after fitting the unknown track position/direction and accounting for scattering and alignment. An outgoing direction alone is insufficient without an additional constraint.

We will report unconstrained muon-only, explicitly vertex-constrained and tracker-combined results separately. The issue records the required pro/con comparison and outstanding validation; this reply does not treat the requirement as satisfied.

Three questions/comments:
- Please explain how you estimated the reserved space for the vacuum vessel envelope. For example, how did you determine the scaling with radius?
- Please explain how you calculated the magnetic field. Do you consider a homogeneous current density along the axial length? If not, please modify the considered detector geometries and parameters to consider homogeneous current density in the magnet windings.
- Please disregard the configuration with a second Solenoid for returning the magnetic field.

@mgtmentink Thank you. Addressed in revision `e6a1ba796bb642f27cd3804519906d1f156422fd`, with the [full response and derivation](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e6a1ba796bb642f27cd3804519906d1f156422fd/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-magnet-expert-review.md) and an updated PR description.

**1. Vacuum-vessel envelope and scaling.** There was no calculated vacuum-vessel radius scaling behind the quoted widths. The inner 0.40 m shell was a planning sum: 0.10 m inner cryostat/interfaces, 0.15 m cold assembly, 0.10 m outer cryostat/support interfaces and 0.05 m margin. The outer 0.50 m shell was also an unverified reservation. These widths include gaps and interfaces; they are not vessel-wall thicknesses.

The earlier `t ∝ B²R` estimate came from magnetic pressure `p=B²/(2μ0)` and ideal hoop loading `t=pR/σ_allow`, applied crudely to historical cold-mass widths. It does **not** size the vacuum enclosure. The response now makes that limitation explicit. Actual vessel sizing still needs separate inner/outer shell and end-closure pressure/load cases, material properties, stiffeners/unsupported lengths, fabrication imperfections, supports, penetrations and thermal clearances. No structurally justified wall thickness or guaranteed enclosure fit can be supplied from the present work.

**2. Field calculation and homogeneous winding current.** The previous calculation used a uniform azimuthal **surface current** on an infinitesimally thin cylinder. It had no radial winding thickness. I have added explicit finite winding packs with **constant azimuthal pack-average J throughout each pack**:

| Main winding | Winding r [m] | Full length [m] | J [A/mm²] | NI [MA-turn] |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Inner | 1.34–1.44 | 6.60 | 25.905 | 17.097 |
| Outer | 4.40–4.60 | 13.00 | 14.518 | 37.747 |

Each coil is separately normalized to +3 T centrally in vacuum; “homogeneous” refers to its spatial current distribution, not equal J between different coils. The inner pack leaves 0.05 m of the former cold-assembly allowance for support/cooling. The outer pack leaves 0.10 m inner cryostat/interfaces, 0.10 m support/cooling and 0.10 m outer cryostat/interfaces within the existing host. All subdivisions are unsigned study choices, not an engineering proof. The inner winding midpoint moves 25 mm inward relative to the old sheet; that change is included explicitly in the comparison.

The code integrates Biot–Savart in radius, z and azimuth, with loop current `dI=J dρ dz`. Independent central normalization uses `B0=μ0 J h[asinh(b/h)−asinh(a/h)]`; `NI=J(b−a)2h`. [Code, inputs and reproduction](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e6a1ba796bb642f27cd3804519906d1f156422fd/tools/magnetic_study/README.md) and [numerical results](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e6a1ba796bb642f27cd3804519906d1f156422fd/docs/validation/DES-004-finite-winding-benchmark.json) are retained. Seven new field tests and all twelve benchmark samples passed; current drawings show the finite winding volumes.

These J values are winding-pack averages, not strand-current densities or demonstrated conductor margins. The current calculation remains a vacuum control. Nonlinear iron and discrete toroid fields have not been solved; those models must use explicit homogeneous winding packs and re-normalize the complete field. Interior/near-winding evaluation and full transport maps remain outside the validated numerical domain.

**3. Active-return configuration.** MAG-06 has been withdrawn from the active comparison, generated comparison figures and next-work recommendations. I interpreted “active solenoid” as the active-return/shielding configuration. Its old card, inputs and evidence remain clearly historical; MAG-01–05 remain under study.

The PR now distinguishes the completed numerical/model amendment from the open vacuum-vessel and magnet engineering questions. No design approval or review closure is inferred from this response.

Please comment on how you determined the length of the cold mass with respect to the length of the vacuum vessel.

Please consider the constraints listed below, implement them in all the detector geometries (now and in the future), and give feedback on how you implemented them in the currently considered detector geometries.

* For the distance from the inner radius of the vacuum vessel RVi to the inner radius of the cold mass RCMi, implement the following scaling relationship: RCMi=RVi*1.065+0.0072 m. This scaling relationship is derived from the technical designs of the ATLAS Central Solenoid and the Compact Muon Solenoid.
* For the thickness of the cold mass itself, we also consider the cold mass outer radius RCMo. To determine the correct thickness of the cold mass (i.e. RCMo-RCMi), we need to know the stored magnetic energy produced by this magnet in energized state (see for example "Wikipedia Magnetic Energy", where "Stored Magnetic Energy" is the magnetic energy stored in the magnetic field). Then, for a given stored magnetic energy, update the outer radius of the cold mass such that the stored magnetic energy is equal to 30 MJ/m^3 times the cold mass volume. Note that this scaling relation is derived from the technical design of the Compact Muon Solenoid.
* For the outer radius of the vacuum vessel RVo, consider the following scaling relationship: RVo = RCMo + 1.75 * (RCMi- RVi). Note that this scaling relationship is based on the technical design of the Compact Muon Solenoid.
* For each of the detector geometries, add a hard constraint where the magnetic field produced in the center of the detector is at or below 5 T. This constraint is given by the practical upper limit of the typical Nb-Ti conductor technology used for building superconducting detector magnets. In general for superconducting detector magnets, a magnetic field magnitude between 1 and 4 T in their free bores is preferable for reasons of engineering practicality.

Implemented the new constraints in `2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645`; [full response, derivation and per-geometry feedback](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-magnet-sizing-review.md).

**Axial lengths:** they were not obtained from vessel engineering. The 6.60/13.00 m winding lengths were inherited field-study hypotheses; the 7.10/13.60 m vessel lengths added provisional 0.25/0.30 m allowances at each end. Cold-mass length is now separately explicit and provisionally equals winding length. Supports, end turns/leads, shields, cooldown movement and closures remain inputs needed to justify those allowances.

**Radial and energy rules:** implemented the inner scaling exactly and iterated finite homogeneous windings/current normalization/cold thickness until `U/Vcold = 30 MJ/m³`. U is the computed all-space vacuum stored energy, not the old uniform-bore proxy. The source integral is equivalent to integrating B²/(2μ0) over all space; the derivation, refinement and independent long-solenoid limit tests are retained. A provisional two-thirds winding / one-third cold support radial split closes the geometry problem.

At +3 T:

| Family | Stored energy | Cold radii [m] | Vessel radii [m] |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Inner (MAG-01/02/05) | 132.576 MJ | 1.327800–1.405769 | 1.240000–1.559419 |
| Outer (MAG-03/04) | 3624.582 MJ | 4.586700–4.898584 | 4.300000–5.400309 |

**Please confirm one notation point:** your outer-radius expression uses undefined `RCM`. I provisionally interpreted it as `RCMi`, so the outer allowance is 1.75 times the inner cold-mass/vessel separation. That assumption is explicit in the policy and remains unconfirmed.

All five active layouts and drawings are updated. MAG-03/04 muon hosts/budgets move outward by 0.600309 m, preserving radial depths and 0.15 m vessel clearance; their maximum radii become 8.100309/10.600309 m. The smaller inner vessel leaves the freed space unassigned. MAG-06 remains withdrawn.

The **5 T central-magnitude cap** is enforced in the current field/geometry tools; 1–4 T remains preferred and all current controls use 3 T. AGENTS.md and CI persist the constraints for future work. The complete installed field must be checked after adding steel or additional magnets: these vacuum results are not complete-system energy sizing or peak-conductor-field certification. In particular, the inner pack now requires about 49.6 A/mm²; conductor margin and the winding/support split need review.

26 magnetic tests, twelve new field samples and all five geometry checks pass, along with dashboard/logging checks. The tracking merge conflict is also resolved, preserving both independent record sets. Expert confirmation and the remaining full-field/engineering inputs remain open; no sign-off or condition closure has been recorded.

issues.title: Evaluate muon return-field versus dedicated-magnet tradeoffs
issues.body:
## Executive summary

Compare muon momentum measurement using the return field of an outer solenoid with a dedicated muon magnet. The physics assessment is that **an instrumented return field can provide an independent muon measurement if sufficient bending is sampled by independent muon measurements**. A separate excitation circuit is not required for measurement independence. Conversely, a large main-solenoid field does not establish standalone capability when the muon stations only measure an outgoing segment beyond it.

This is a **DRAFT research follow-up to PR #6 / DES-004**, not a baseline-update issue or topology selection. No nODD muon momentum resolution has been demonstrated. Human review must first agree which fit classes and performance criteria are required.

## Scope and evidence

The following tradeoffs are **INFERENCE**, grounded in the registered sources and measurement arguments in the [muon assessment](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/research/magnetic-configurations/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-muon.md#public-evidence-and-next-gate) and [physics protocol](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/research/magnetic-configurations/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-physics-validation.md#4-observables-and-fair-controls). Current allocations are the [stepped candidate envelopes](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/research/magnetic-configurations/docs/design/DES-004-magnetic-configurations.md#candidate-specific-muon-envelopes), not the original fixed E1-R2 hosts.

| Candidate | Potential advantages | Costs / unresolved physics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MAG-01: inner solenoid, no dedicated yoke | Compact central-magnet control; tracker information can support a combined fit. | Outer curvature may be weak or poorly observed. An outgoing segment alone cannot separate unknown incoming direction from momentum. Unconstrained standalone capability remains a question to calculate, not an assumed impossibility. |
| MAG-03: outer solenoid, no dedicated yoke | Main-field bending before outer measurements may help tracker-combined or vertex-constrained fits; avoids a dedicated massive yoke. | Unconfined fringe/return flux does not guarantee useful curvature between muon measurements. Stray field, forward orientation and the material of calorimeters, coil and supports remain relevant. |
| MAG-04: outer solenoid, instrumented iron return | Return flux can supply bending among muon measurements without a separate muon coil; CMS provides a built topology precedent. | Steel, air gaps and nonlinear response determine the field; scattering, energy loss and stopping compete with bending. Requires space, alignment, field calibration and end-return design. A stronger local field alone is not proof of a better fit. |
| MAG-05: inner solenoid plus air-core toroids | Intended bending within the muon spectrometer; field orientation can help forward trajectories. Avoids scattering in a dedicated return yoke; ATLAS provides a built topology precedent. | Additional coils, cryostats, supports and services; sector-dependent field and obstructions. Station lever arms, alignment and barrel/endcap transitions must work at nODD's scale. |
| MAG-06: outer main solenoid plus active return | An instrumented return annulus can combine distributed bending with less dedicated iron; external-field control is an explicit objective. | Trades iron for coupled coils, supports, cryogenics and protection. Finite ends, return-current choice, forward leverage and shared service space are unresolved. The fourth-concept precedent is a proposal, not operating evidence. |

MAG-02 (inner solenoid with an instrumented iron return) remains a useful companion control: it separates changing main-coil scale from adding an instrumented return. All options must include inherited calorimeter/support steel in their physical field model; “no dedicated yoke” does not mean an iron-free detector.

**FACT anchors already catalogued:** SRC-ATLAS-JINST-2008 §6.1, printed p.164/PDF194 and Figs.6.1–6.2/PDF195; SRC-CMS-YOKE-COSMICS-2010 §§1–2/PDF3–5; SRC-CMS-FIELD-MAP-2023 §§1–2/PDF2–3. SRC-FOURTH-CONCEPT-2007 §2.3/PDF5 and Fig.5/PDF6 supplies the active-return concept; its quoted angular reach corresponds to |eta|≈2.185 and does not establish the nODD |eta|<3 goal or 3.5 stretch. Source identities and public links: [manifest](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/research/magnetic-configurations/reference/manifest.yaml). These precedents establish mechanisms and modeling obligations, not transferable nODD performance.

## Discriminating study and deliverables

**NODD DESIGN CHOICE — proposed study, human approval pending:** use the existing physics protocol and validation catalogue, with four separately reported fit classes:

1. Tracker-only.
2. Muon-only unconstrained standalone: no tracker hits or interaction-point prior.
3. Muon-only with an explicit vertex prior and uncertainty.
4. Tracker–muon combined: state any vertex prior separately.

- [ ] Physics + muon engineer: agree momentum, charge, eta/phi, prompt/displaced samples, measurement errors, alignment scenarios, required coverage and acceptance criteria before ranking candidates. Reuse the recorded diagnostic grid; do not invent performance thresholds from results.
- [ ] System architect + software: establish verified vector fields (finite coils first; nonlinear iron where applicable), domain/uncertainty policies and field-map/direct-evaluation agreement. For MAG-06, test finite dual coils and then end-return variants rather than treating flux-area arithmetic as a field solution.
- [ ] Muon engineer + software: place explicit independent measurement surfaces within the current stepped hosts; retain service/coil exclusions. Show both common diagnostic controls and physically candidate-specific station layouts, identifying their different resource costs.
- [ ] Physics + software: calculate crossings, signed vector bending and displacement response to q/p between measurements; examine which momentum information remains after fitting the unknown initial position/direction. Opposing bends may cancel net deflection while retaining measurable intermediate displacement. Neither an unsigned field integral nor host length is a resolution.
- [ ] Physics + software: move from vacuum controls to fixed-material comparisons and then physical candidate-dependent material/measurement fits. Report charge determination, momentum residuals/pulls, efficiency and failure fractions versus eta/phi/momentum; distinguish surviving-track precision from survival probability. Test field/alignment uncertainties and vertex-prior dependence, including displaced particles.
- [ ] Calorimeter + muon engineer: keep leakage/punch-through and background studies separate from momentum fits; do not add iron solely to obtain a desired performance curve.
- [ ] Publication office: record reproducible evidence, uncertainties and a pro/con recommendation in Git under DES-004, linked to FIELD-V01, PROP-V01 and MU-V01–08. If a layout is subsequently selected, open its separate baseline-amendment issue.

## Decision requested

## Executive summary

Retain the research tracks comparing **MAG-01–05** as isolated DES-004 magnetic-layout prototypes; **MAG-06 remains withdrawn** following expert direction. No topology is selected and no production geometry is changed.

The [2026-09-24 expert response](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-magnet-sizing-review.md) implements review-directed vessel gaps, **30 MJ/m³ stored-energy/cold-volume sizing**, and a **hard 5 T central-field cap**, with 1–4 T preferred. Current vacuum controls remain at 3 T and retain homogeneous winding-pack current density. The rules are recorded in AGENTS.md, a central policy, field/layout validators and CI for current and future studies.

| Main-coil family | Vacuum stored energy | Cold-mass radial bounds | Vessel radial bounds | Cold / vessel full length |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| Inner: MAG-01/02/05 | 132.576 MJ | 1.327800–1.405769 m | 1.240000–1.559419 m | 6.60 / 7.10 m |
| Outer: MAG-03/04 | 3624.582 MJ | 4.586700–4.898584 m | 4.300000–5.400309 m | 13.00 / 13.60 m |

**Integration consequence:** the outer-family vessel grows by 0.600309 m radially. MAG-03/04 muon hosts, nested radial budgets and trial steel bands move outward by that amount, preserving their depths and 0.15 m vessel-to-host gap. Overall outer radii become 8.100309 / 10.600309 m. Stepped endcap fronts, beam apertures, tracker and calorimeters stay at their retained study coordinates. All five updated layouts pass positive-intersection and containment checks.

![Updated five-option composite layouts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/asalzburger/nodd/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/docs/design/figures/DES-004-muon-envelopes-comparison-rz.png)

## Expert comments and implementation

- **Axial lengths:** previous end allowances were planning choices, not engineered vessel-length estimates. The current model explicitly sets cold length equal to winding length, with 0.25 / 0.30 m per-end allowances. End supports, leads, shields, cooldown movement and closures still need engineering.
- **Inner radial gap:** enforce `RCMi = 1.065 RVi + 0.0072 m`.
- **Cold thickness:** iterate winding geometry, its uniform current normalization and cold-mass outer radius until calculated stored energy equals 30 MJ/m³ times the annular cold volume. Retain the earlier 2:1 winding/support radial split as an explicit provisional closure.
- **Outer radial gap:** provisionally interpret the undefined `RCM` as `RCMi`, giving `RVo = RCMo + 1.75 (RCMi − RVi)`. **Expert confirmation remains requested.**
- **Field:** reject nonfinite central fields or magnitudes above 5 T. Complete installed fields must obey that cap after adding iron or other magnets; a main-coil vacuum control cannot certify the total field or peak conductor margin.

The new energy calculation integrates the complete vacuum field through the equivalent current/vector-potential source integral, with axial separation integrated analytically. It includes fringe/return energy and avoids a finite map cutoff or a uniform-bore proxy. [Sizing input/code/results](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/docs/validation/DES-004-magnet-sizing.json) retain provenance and refinement. [Reproduction commands](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/tools/magnetic_study/README.md) require no new numerical dependency beyond NumPy.

## Evidence and limits

At the September 24 scientific evidence revision, passed locally: **26 magnetic tests, 26 dashboard tests, 15 logging tests, 5 node-preflight tests and 14 JavaScript assertions**, dashboard validation/build, session validation, input/code hashes and whitespace checks. Energy tests include an independent infinite-solenoid field-energy limit, analytic axial integration, B²/geometric scaling, refinement and rejection cases. All twelve updated field benchmark samples and all five composite geometries pass. Magnetic tests now run in hosted CI.

These are conditional **vacuum main-coil** results. Installed calorimeter/support steel affects every physical candidate; MAG-02/04 need nonlinear iron solutions and MAG-05 needs explicit toroid windings, coupled energy and cold-volume accounting. Inner pack-average J becomes 49.643 A/mm², requiring conductor/protection review. No structural adequacy, peak-field margin, standalone muon performance or full transport map is demonstrated.

The earlier thin-sheet and finite-pack evidence remains historical. The 2026-09-22 finite-winding benchmark is unchanged; new field evidence is separately named. Prior composite reports/drawings remain in Git. The old MAG-06 card is archived, not promoted back into the active comparison.

## Synchronization and accounting — 2026-10-12

Resolved all 26 conflict paths through an ordinary merge of `main` at `ed30e63fb0ab30b66d4084a9058906929006f792`. Retained both source catalogues and all review records by stable ID, including exact reviewed revisions and approval states. All 78 magnetic-study files are byte-identical to the previous PR head. Magnetic regression tests now run in the current Project validation workflow; the retired progress-dashboard workflow remains removed.

The merge brings existing canonical token backfills into this branch: **36 disjoint turns across 11 research session records, 56,250,297 input + 211,577 output = 56,461,874 observed tokens**. They were already counted on main and are not counted again. The device audit found no additional attributable historical PR6 counters. **Token usage for the September 28 PR6 merge-maintenance session is still unavailable on this device**, as are final counters for this active update turn. The now-completed preceding PR62 synchronization turn adds 3,486,578 tokens to its own original session, separate from magnetic research. [Curated audit](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/research/magnetic-configurations/logs/usage/USAGE-2026-10-12-pr6-accounting-audit.json).

Current local validation: **108 Python tests passed** (26 magnetic, 11 envelope, 28 project-record, 33 session-logging and 10 token-site); project records validation; token-site validation/build; session validation and accounting summary. Full whitespace scans report only inherited generated SVG whitespace, verified byte-for-byte against the respective parents; the edited workflow, index, catalogues and records pass. Hosted checks are reported on the published revision.

## Review boundary

This update makes the research record compatible with current main; **no topology decision, selection, design approval or sign-off is recorded**. DES-004 remains DRAFT, the studies remain isolated PROTOTYPE work, and the historical CHANGES_REQUESTED review is preserved. PR6 itself is not merged by this update.

Scientific follow-up remains the provisional `RCMi` interpretation, axial allowances, winding/support closure, conductor margin and complete installed-field validation. Final human sign-off remains with `asalzburger-review`. Related: DES-004, ADR-006 and muon-performance issue #9. Scientific evidence target remains `2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645`; closing the issue or merging the research record does not confer approval.

An independent muon momentum measurement does not inherently require a separately powered muon magnet. Three questions/comments:
- Please explain how you estimated the reserved space for the vacuum vessel envelope. For example, how did you determine the scaling with radius?
- Please explain how you calculated the magnetic field. Do you consider a homogeneous current density along the axial length? If not, please modify the considered detector geometries and parameters to consider homogeneous current density in the magnet windings.
- Please disregard the configuration with a second Solenoid for returning the magnetic field.

@mgtmentink Thank you. Addressed in revision `e6a1ba796bb642f27cd3804519906d1f156422fd`, with the [full response and derivation](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e6a1ba796bb642f27cd3804519906d1f156422fd/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-magnet-expert-review.md) and an updated PR description.

**1. Vacuum-vessel envelope and scaling.** There was no calculated vacuum-vessel radius scaling behind the quoted widths. The inner 0.40 m shell was a planning sum: 0.10 m inner cryostat/interfaces, 0.15 m cold assembly, 0.10 m outer cryostat/support interfaces and 0.05 m margin. The outer 0.50 m shell was also an unverified reservation. These widths include gaps and interfaces; they are not vessel-wall thicknesses.

The earlier `t ∝ B²R` estimate came from magnetic pressure `p=B²/(2μ0)` and ideal hoop loading `t=pR/σ_allow`, applied crudely to historical cold-mass widths. It does **not** size the vacuum enclosure. The response now makes that limitation explicit. Actual vessel sizing still needs separate inner/outer shell and end-closure pressure/load cases, material properties, stiffeners/unsupported lengths, fabrication imperfections, supports, penetrations and thermal clearances. No structurally justified wall thickness or guaranteed enclosure fit can be supplied from the present work.

**2. Field calculation and homogeneous winding current.** The previous calculation used a uniform azimuthal **surface current** on an infinitesimally thin cylinder. It had no radial winding thickness. I have added explicit finite winding packs with **constant azimuthal pack-average J throughout each pack**:

| Main winding | Winding r [m] | Full length [m] | J [A/mm²] | NI [MA-turn] |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Inner | 1.34–1.44 | 6.60 | 25.905 | 17.097 |
| Outer | 4.40–4.60 | 13.00 | 14.518 | 37.747 |

Each coil is separately normalized to +3 T centrally in vacuum; “homogeneous” refers to its spatial current distribution, not equal J between different coils. The inner pack leaves 0.05 m of the former cold-assembly allowance for support/cooling. The outer pack leaves 0.10 m inner cryostat/interfaces, 0.10 m support/cooling and 0.10 m outer cryostat/interfaces within the existing host. All subdivisions are unsigned study choices, not an engineering proof. The inner winding midpoint moves 25 mm inward relative to the old sheet; that change is included explicitly in the comparison.

The code integrates Biot–Savart in radius, z and azimuth, with loop current `dI=J dρ dz`. Independent central normalization uses `B0=μ0 J h[asinh(b/h)−asinh(a/h)]`; `NI=J(b−a)2h`. [Code, inputs and reproduction](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e6a1ba796bb642f27cd3804519906d1f156422fd/tools/magnetic_study/README.md) and [numerical results](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/e6a1ba796bb642f27cd3804519906d1f156422fd/docs/validation/DES-004-finite-winding-benchmark.json) are retained. Seven new field tests and all twelve benchmark samples passed; current drawings show the finite winding volumes.

These J values are winding-pack averages, not strand-current densities or demonstrated conductor margins. The current calculation remains a vacuum control. Nonlinear iron and discrete toroid fields have not been solved; those models must use explicit homogeneous winding packs and re-normalize the complete field. Interior/near-winding evaluation and full transport maps remain outside the validated numerical domain.

**3. Active-return configuration.** MAG-06 has been withdrawn from the active comparison, generated comparison figures and next-work recommendations. I interpreted “active solenoid” as the active-return/shielding configuration. Its old card, inputs and evidence remain clearly historical; MAG-01–05 remain under study.

The PR now distinguishes the completed numerical/model amendment from the open vacuum-vessel and magnet engineering questions. No design approval or review closure is inferred from this response.

Please comment on how you determined the length of the cold mass with respect to the length of the vacuum vessel.

Please consider the constraints listed below, implement them in all the detector geometries (now and in the future), and give feedback on how you implemented them in the currently considered detector geometries.

* For the distance from the inner radius of the vacuum vessel RVi to the inner radius of the cold mass RCMi, implement the following scaling relationship: RCMi=RVi*1.065+0.0072 m. This scaling relationship is derived from the technical designs of the ATLAS Central Solenoid and the Compact Muon Solenoid.
* For the thickness of the cold mass itself, we also consider the cold mass outer radius RCMo. To determine the correct thickness of the cold mass (i.e. RCMo-RCMi), we need to know the stored magnetic energy produced by this magnet in energized state (see for example "Wikipedia Magnetic Energy", where "Stored Magnetic Energy" is the magnetic energy stored in the magnetic field). Then, for a given stored magnetic energy, update the outer radius of the cold mass such that the stored magnetic energy is equal to 30 MJ/m^3 times the cold mass volume. Note that this scaling relation is derived from the technical design of the Compact Muon Solenoid.
* For the outer radius of the vacuum vessel RVo, consider the following scaling relationship: RVo = RCMo + 1.75 * (RCMi- RVi). Note that this scaling relationship is based on the technical design of the Compact Muon Solenoid.
* For each of the detector geometries, add a hard constraint where the magnetic field produced in the center of the detector is at or below 5 T. This constraint is given by the practical upper limit of the typical Nb-Ti conductor technology used for building superconducting detector magnets. In general for superconducting detector magnets, a magnetic field magnitude between 1 and 4 T in their free bores is preferable for reasons of engineering practicality.

Implemented the new constraints in `2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645`; [full response, derivation and per-geometry feedback](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/2b8c032fb9c6e8aa2333ae5a4c88818cacecc645/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-magnet-sizing-review.md).

**Axial lengths:** they were not obtained from vessel engineering. The 6.60/13.00 m winding lengths were inherited field-study hypotheses; the 7.10/13.60 m vessel lengths added provisional 0.25/0.30 m allowances at each end. Cold-mass length is now separately explicit and provisionally equals winding length. Supports, end turns/leads, shields, cooldown movement and closures remain inputs needed to justify those allowances.

**Radial and energy rules:** implemented the inner scaling exactly and iterated finite homogeneous windings/current normalization/cold thickness until `U/Vcold = 30 MJ/m³`. U is the computed all-space vacuum stored energy, not the old uniform-bore proxy. The source integral is equivalent to integrating B²/(2μ0) over all space; the derivation, refinement and independent long-solenoid limit tests are retained. A provisional two-thirds winding / one-third cold support radial split closes the geometry problem.

At +3 T:

| Family | Stored energy | Cold radii [m] | Vessel radii [m] |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| Inner (MAG-01/02/05) | 132.576 MJ | 1.327800–1.405769 | 1.240000–1.559419 |
| Outer (MAG-03/04) | 3624.582 MJ | 4.586700–4.898584 | 4.300000–5.400309 |

**Please confirm one notation point:** your outer-radius expression uses undefined `RCM`. I provisionally interpreted it as `RCMi`, so the outer allowance is 1.75 times the inner cold-mass/vessel separation. That assumption is explicit in the policy and remains unconfirmed.

All five active layouts and drawings are updated. MAG-03/04 muon hosts/budgets move outward by 0.600309 m, preserving radial depths and 0.15 m vessel clearance; their maximum radii become 8.100309/10.600309 m. The smaller inner vessel leaves the freed space unassigned. MAG-06 remains withdrawn.

The **5 T central-magnitude cap** is enforced in the current field/geometry tools; 1–4 T remains preferred and all current controls use 3 T. AGENTS.md and CI persist the constraints for future work. The complete installed field must be checked after adding steel or additional magnets: these vacuum results are not complete-system energy sizing or peak-conductor-field certification. In particular, the inner pack now requires about 49.6 A/mm²; conductor margin and the winding/support split need review.

26 magnetic tests, twelve new field samples and all five geometry checks pass, along with dashboard/logging checks. The tracking merge conflict is also resolved, preserving both independent record sets. Expert confirmation and the remaining full-field/engineering inputs remain open; no sign-off or condition closure has been recorded.

## Executive summary

Compare muon momentum measurement using the return field of an outer solenoid with a dedicated muon magnet. The physics assessment is that **an instrumented return field can provide an independent muon measurement if sufficient bending is sampled by independent muon measurements**. A separate excitation circuit is not required for measurement independence. Conversely, a large main-solenoid field does not establish standalone capability when the muon stations only measure an outgoing segment beyond it.

This is a **DRAFT research follow-up to PR #6 / DES-004**, not a baseline-update issue or topology selection. No nODD muon momentum resolution has been demonstrated. Human review must first agree which fit classes and performance criteria are required.

## Scope and evidence

The following tradeoffs are **INFERENCE**, grounded in the registered sources and measurement arguments in the [muon assessment](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/research/magnetic-configurations/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-muon.md#public-evidence-and-next-gate) and [physics protocol](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/research/magnetic-configurations/docs/design/inputs/DES-004-physics-validation.md#4-observables-and-fair-controls). Current allocations are the [stepped candidate envelopes](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/blob/research/magnetic-configurations/docs/design/DES-004-magnetic-configurations.md#candidate-specific-muon-envelopes), not the original fixed E1-R2 hosts.

| Candidate | Potential advantages | Costs / unresolved physics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MAG-01: inner solenoid, no dedicated yoke | Compact central-magnet control; tracker information can support a combined fit. | Outer curvature may be weak or poorly observed. An outgoing segment alone cannot separate unknown incoming direction from momentum. Unconstrained standalone capability remains a question to calculate, not an assumed impossibility. |
| MAG-03: outer solenoid, no dedicated yoke | Main-field bending before outer measurements may help tracker-combined or vertex-constrained fits; avoids a dedicated massive yoke. | Unconfined fringe/return flux does not guarantee useful curvature between muon measurements. Stray field, forward orientation and the material of calorimeters, coil and supports remain relevant. |
| MAG-04: outer solenoid, instrumented iron return | Return flux can supply bending among muon measurements without a separate muon coil; CMS provides a built topology precedent. | Steel, air gaps and nonlinear response determine the field; scattering, energy loss and stopping compete with bending. Requires space, alignment, field calibration and end-return design. A stronger local field alone is not proof of a better fit. |
| MAG-05: inner solenoid plus air-core toroids | Intended bending within the muon spectrometer; field orientation can help forward trajectories. Avoids scattering in a dedicated return yoke; ATLAS provides a built topology precedent. | Additional coils, cryostats, supports and services; sector-dependent field and obstructions. Station lever arms, alignment and barrel/endcap transitions must work at nODD's scale. |
| MAG-06: outer main solenoid plus active return | An instrumented return annulus can combine distributed bending with less dedicated iron; external-field control is an explicit objective. | Trades iron for coupled coils, supports, cryogenics and protection. Finite ends, return-current choice, forward leverage and shared service space are unresolved. The fourth-concept precedent is a proposal, not operating evidence. |

MAG-02 (inner solenoid with an instrumented iron return) remains a useful companion control: it separates changing main-coil scale from adding an instrumented return. All options must include inherited calorimeter/support steel in their physical field model; “no dedicated yoke” does not mean an iron-free detector.

## Discriminating study and deliverables

**NODD DESIGN CHOICE — proposed study, human approval pending:** use the existing physics protocol and validation catalogue, with four separately reported fit classes:

1. Tracker-only.
2. Muon-only unconstrained standalone: no tracker hits or interaction-point prior.
3. Muon-only with an explicit vertex prior and uncertainty.
4. Tracker–muon combined: state any vertex prior separately.

- [ ] Physics + muon engineer: agree momentum, charge, eta/phi, prompt/displaced samples, measurement errors, alignment scenarios, required coverage and acceptance criteria before ranking candidates. Reuse the recorded diagnostic grid; do not invent performance thresholds from results.
- [ ] System architect + software: establish verified vector fields (finite coils first; nonlinear iron where applicable), domain/uncertainty policies and field-map/direct-evaluation agreement. For MAG-06, test finite dual coils and then end-return variants rather than treating flux-area arithmetic as a field solution.
- [ ] Muon engineer + software: place explicit independent measurement surfaces within the current stepped hosts; retain service/coil exclusions. Show both common diagnostic controls and physically candidate-specific station layouts, identifying their different resource costs.
- [ ] Physics + software: calculate crossings, signed vector bending and displacement response to q/p between measurements; examine which momentum information remains after fitting the unknown initial position/direction. Opposing bends may cancel net deflection while retaining measurable intermediate displacement. Neither an unsigned field integral nor host length is a resolution.
- [ ] Physics + software: move from vacuum controls to fixed-material comparisons and then physical candidate-dependent material/measurement fits. Report charge determination, momentum residuals/pulls, efficiency and failure fractions versus eta/phi/momentum; distinguish surviving-track precision from survival probability. Test field/alignment uncertainties and vertex-prior dependence, including displaced particles.
- [ ] Calorimeter + muon engineer: keep leakage/punch-through and background studies separate from momentum fits; do not add iron solely to obtain a desired performance curve.
